# Rust Instructions

These instructions define the coding conventions for Rust in this workspace.

## Language Version

Rust 2021 edition, rust-version 1.75

## Error Handling

* Define error types with `thiserror` for library code
* Use `anyhow` only in binary and test code
* Propagate with `?` and add context via `.context()`
* Never `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` in library code without proof comment

## Naming Conventions

* `snake_case` for variables, functions, methods, modules, crate names
* `PascalCase` for types, traits, enum variants
* `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for constants and statics
* Prefix private helper functions with `_` only when disambiguation is needed

## Code Organization

* One module per file; use directories for module hierarchies
* `pub(crate)` as default visibility; `pub` only for public API
* Group imports: std → external crates → internal modules
* Place `mod` declarations at top of `lib.rs`/`main.rs`

## Documentation

* `///` doc comments on all public items
* `//!` module-level doc comments on every module
* Include code examples for complex public APIs
* Document panics, safety, and error conditions

## Testing

* TDD: write tests before implementation
* Unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` within source modules
* Integration tests in `tests/` directory
* Property-based testing with `proptest` for wide-domain inputs
* Trait-based mocking with `mockall` at module boundaries

## Dependencies

* Pin dependencies to exact versions in `Cargo.lock`
* Use `cargo audit` to check for known vulnerabilities
* Prefer well-maintained crates with recent activity
* Minimize dependency count; avoid pulling in large crates for small utilities

## Safety & Security

* `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` at crate root
* Every `unsafe` block requires `// SAFETY:` justification
* Prefer safe abstractions over raw pointer manipulation
* Use `std::mem::ManuallyDrop` over `std::mem::forget` when ownership transfer is explicit

## Performance

* Prefer `&str` over `String` in function parameters
* Use `Cow<'_, str>` when allocation is conditional
* Avoid `.clone()` without justification; prefer borrowing
* Use `Vec::with_capacity()` when size is known
* Profile before optimizing; use `cargo flamegraph` or `criterion`

## Anti-Patterns

The following patterns are prohibited:

* `.unwrap()` / `.expect()` in library code without proof
* `unsafe` without `// SAFETY:` comment
* `.clone()` without justification
* Holding a mutex lock across `.await`
* Raw string SQL in embedded DB queries
* `std::process::exit()` in library code
